port `src/` — "we'll probably have better designs now anyway." Preferred
approach: move legacy out to an archive path and fix forward one module at a
time rather than re-importing.

### Measured state

NOT STARTED**, and line 10 asserts "no startup command references `server/`".
**That assertion is now false.** The live local service runs

`scripts/local-clone-autostart.sh:66-70`). The cutover half-happened outside
the charter's sequence.

`server/` today is a transport and tool layer on top of the legacy core.

### Reachability, measured transitively

Starting from the `src/` modules `server/` imports and following their own

```
reachable from server/main.ts : 122 modules   43,142 lines
NOT reachable                 :  26 modules   11,014 lines
src/ total (non-test)         : 148 modules   54,156 lines
both trees together           :               78,410 lines
```

**~80% of the legacy tree is live under the running server.** An earlier

### The dependency is CIRCULAR

```
src/index.ts:7   imports ../server/transport/server-identity.ts
src/index.ts:49  imports ../server/observability/langfuse-tracing.ts
```

The old tree depends on the new tree while the new tree depends on the old.
Neither side detaches cleanly, and the circular edge must be cut before

### Why this is a defect generator

`src/tools/index.ts` — which `server/main.ts` imports — re-exports
`agent-context-pack`, `brain-answer`, `get-contract`, and `scan-namespace`,
which ALSO exist under `server/tools/`. Both copies are reachable, both
compile, and a direct-path grep does not reveal which one serves.

Measured cost this session: #747 required fixing the same defect in both trees
across four edits, and the #744 done-means gate has to drive **both** trees
in-process because the deciding line was byte-identical in each. A fix landed
in the wrong twin looks fixed and is not — a direct contributor to the
four-defect chain in #747 going unnoticed for 27 days.

Attempted and correctly refused this session: archiving the "dead" twins. 16 of
23 twinned tool files appear unreferenced by direct path, but four are reached
through the `src/tools/index.ts` barrel and two more are imported directly by
`server/`. **Archiving any of them today breaks the running service.**

### Why the line count is what it is

Three causes, largest first. This is diagnosis, not a cleanup mandate.

1. **The application exists twice** — 78,410 lines across both trees for one

2. **Multi-concern modules** — repo standard is 500 code lines/file

### Scope

Rewrite each concern natively in `server/`, then drop the `src/` import. New

Sequencing:

1. Cut the circular edge (`src/index.ts` → `server/`).
2. Archive the 26 unreachable modules; verify the service still starts and the

3. Work the reachable 122 one concern at a time, following the import census:

## Rewritten: enforcement first, splitting last

Operator ruling 2026-08-25: bring this repo to the Development coding
standards, and finish the rewrite inside `server/` rather than porting `src/`.

The original framing of this issue put the rewrite first. That is the wrong
order and `_DOCS/CODING_STANDARDS.md:637-660` says so directly:

> **Do not attempt a single sweeping "bring it up to standard" change.** It
> produces an unreviewable diff, mixes mechanical reformatting with real
> behavioural fixes, and — the common failure — **lands the rules before the
> mechanism that keeps them, so the repo drifts straight back.**

Its fixed order, each step on its own branch and PR: **1. enforcement
(hooks) → 2. formatter/linter → 3. type checking → 4. validated config →
5. documentation → 6. split oversized files.** Splitting is LAST.

`STANDARDS-python.md:20-58` supplies the definition this plan uses throughout:

> **A rule is only as real as the mechanism that fires.** LAW means a hook
> fails the commit. If no hook enforces it, it is not a law and must not be
> written as one.

By that definition this repo currently has **two laws**: protected-branch and
gitleaks.

## The two structural problems this must fix

**1. The application exists twice, and the halves have diverged.**
122 of 148 `src/` modules (43,142 lines) are transitively reachable from
`server/main.ts`. Twinned tool files are not copies — `agent-context-pack.ts`
is 1,647 lines in `src/` vs 988 in `server/`, 1,299 differing lines;
`ingest-conversation-facts.ts` 803 vs 447; `ingest-raw-turn.ts` 410 vs 148.
Two implementations of the same tool, both compiling.

Confirmed this session: `server/main.ts:83` imports `src/tools/index.ts` as
`import type` only and never calls `registerAllTools`, so `server/` registers
its own tool copies exclusively. The `src/tools/` twins are not on the runtime
path even though they compile and typecheck.

**2. The dependency is circular.**
```
src/index.ts:7   imports ../server/transport/server-identity.ts
src/index.ts:49  imports ../server/observability/langfuse-tracing.ts
```
Neither side detaches until this is cut.

**Measured cost:** #747 was one logical defect that took four edits across both
trees. The #744 done-means gate has to boot both trees in-process because the
deciding line was byte-identical in each. A fix landed in the wrong twin looks
fixed and is not — a direct contributor to that four-defect chain surviving 27
days.

For scope accuracy: cause 3 is under 1,000 of the 78,000 lines. `zod` is

## Plan

`_DOCS/typescript-exemplar/` **exists** and is complete — `.oxlintrc.json`,
`_githooks/`, CI, and `tests/enforcement.test.ts` that proves each size rule
fires. (`STANDARDS-typescript.md:9` and `:619` both claim it does not exist;
the doc is stale and should be corrected.) It is the template for steps 1-2
rather than something to design.

**Step 1 — enforcement.** Extend `_githooks/pre-commit` beyond branch+gitleaks
to run lint and typecheck on staged content, matching the exemplar's
staged-index approach and its fail-closed posture. CI runs the same commands
over the same paths (`CODING_STANDARDS.md:495-499`). Verify by making a
deliberately non-compliant commit that MUST fail.

**Step 2 — linter/formatter.** Adopt the exemplar's `.oxlintrc.json` and
`.prettierrc.json`. Purely mechanical; lands alone; reviewed by confirming the
test suite is unchanged. Port `tests/enforcement.test.ts` so the rules are
proven to fire here, not assumed.

**Step 3 — type checking.** Add `erasableSyntaxOnly`; convert the 20
`namespace` declarations; narrow the 38 `any`s per-module rather than blanket
ignoring.

**Step 4 — validated config.** One module, schema-validated at boot, exits on
invalid input. Retires 30 scattered `process.env` readers.

**Step 5 — documentation.** TSDoc on public surfaces.

**Step 6 — structure.** Cut the circular edge, then rewrite each concern
natively in `server/` and drop its `src/` import, following the import census:
types/namespace primitives → logging/observability → embedding → maintenance
queue + sweep → NATS → REST → contract → source registry → tools. New
implementation against current design, not a port. Retire `src/` and update
`package.json` `start`.

Multi-session program. Per `_DOCS/HANDOFF-BASE.md` each step decomposes into
small bounded lanes with a deliverable, scope, non-goals, and an executable
done-means check.

### The done-check, proven RED first

Staging a file containing an explicit `any` and a non-null assertion:

```
[pre-commit] oxlint (staged content)
  .../pre-commit-staged-50257/src/__redcheck.ts:2:12
    error typescript(no-explicit-any)
  .../pre-commit-staged-50257/src/__redcheck.ts:3:10
    error typescript(no-non-null-assertion)
[pre-commit] BLOCKED. Nothing was committed.
```

Rejected by rule name, against the **staged copy** in a temp tree — not the
working tree. Checking the working tree is the common way a hook lies: stage a
fix, leave a broken edit unstaged, and it passes on code that is not what you
are committing.

It then blocked its own author. The `d3df0fd` commit was refused on a prettier
violation in `tests/enforcement.test.ts` and only landed after the fix.

### Every numeric rule is live, not inert

Head-verified independently of the lane that wrote the config. Tightening each
value by exactly one makes it report:

```
2 complexity · 1 max-depth · 1 max-lines
1 max-lines-per-function · 4 max-params
```

They sit exactly at the tree's current worst case with no slack:
`max-lines 1849 · max-lines-per-function 535 · complexity 129 · max-params 11
· max-depth 5`. No rule is disabled and none dropped from the exemplar's set.

Loose values are the deliberate migration posture — a rule failing on 40 files
on day one is a rule someone deletes. Session 4 lowers them one notch at a
time and fixes what breaks.

### The test cannot pass by accident

Every limit is read at run time via `bunx oxlint --print-config`, so no value
is duplicated into the test; the first ratchet would otherwise leave it
silently testing numbers nobody uses. Each test asserts the rule NAME appears,
not merely a non-zero exit.

Proven honest rather than assumed: widening `max-params` to 999 in a scratch
copy silences the rule against the same 12-parameter fixture, while the real
config reports it.

Two defects were found and fixed during the build, both of which would have
made the file misleading rather than merely wrong:

1. `lint()` and `typecheck()` shared one scratch filename. bun runs tests in a
   file concurrently, so one test overwrote another's snippet mid-flight. The
   symptom was a rule reporting a violation from a different test's fixture —
   indistinguishable from "the rule was disabled", which is the single
   conclusion this file has to get right.
2. The `max-lines` counter-test asserted something false: its "compliant"
   fixture was ~32 code lines over the limit, so the rule was correctly firing
   and the test was demanding it not.
